title: Trend, Seasonality, Cycles & Remainder
interviewAnswer: A time series can contain trend, seasonal patterns, longer cycles and irregular remainder. I identify these structures before selecting a model because validation and feature construction depend on them.
keyPoints: Seasonality has a known calendar frequency; cycles need not.
why: Trend, Seasonality, Cycles & Remainder appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: A time series can contain trend, seasonal patterns, longer cycles and irregular remainder. I identify these structures before selecting a model because validation and feature construction depend on them. Seasonality has a known calendar frequency; cycles need not. Multiple seasonalities can coexist. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Hourly demand may have daily and weekly seasonality plus a long-term growth trend.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Trend, Seasonality, Cycles & Remainder make?
How would you validate or debug Trend, Seasonality, Cycles & Remainder in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
